findings.title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive
findings.body: `should_block?` uses an exact `where(email: email)` lookup and nothing normalizes the stored or incoming address. A blocked address can therefore be bypassed by changing its case, for example 'Bad@Spam.org' instead of 'bad@spam.org'. Both the stored and queried values should be downcased (e.g. with Email.downcase).

findings.title: Non-atomic match_count increment as a side effect of validation
findings.body: The method does a read, then `+= 1`, then `save`. Concurrent signups attempting the same email lose increments. It also writes to the DB on every `valid?` call: the users controller calls `valid?` and then `save`, so each signup attempt is counted twice. Use an atomic `update_all('match_count = match_count + 1')`, or `increment_counter`.

findings.title: rejectedEmails array shared across all controller instances
findings.body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is defined on the prototype in `extend`, so every instance shares one array. Rejected emails persist across modal instances. It should be initialized in `init`.

findings.title: Rejected email recorded for any email error, including uniqueness
findings.body: The client adds the email to `rejectedEmails` whenever `errors.email` is present. That includes an email-taken uniqueness error and transient whitelist errors. The user is then permanently told the email is 'invalid', which is a misleading message.
